01Dashboard SummaryOverview▶

This dashboard documents Export Selected to DXF (v1.0.0), a Fusion palette add-in that exports whatever you have selected — sketch curves, whole sketches, planar faces and flat patterns — as one DXF file per item. Sections 02–06 reproduce the build handoff verbatim; sections 07–11 add reference material: what the add-in accepts, every option and its default, the package contents, how each export path works, and a test checklist. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Start hereExport Selected to DXF (v1.0.0) is built. It passed its preflight checks, and the add-in button goes in DESIGN under SOLID ▸ CREATE and UTILITIES ▸ ADD-INS. To get it running, go straight to Install & Shortcut.

02What It DoesFeature▶

The top of the panel stays visible and shows your current selection, updating as you select things, for example "38 selected → 4 files · 4 sketches". Below that is a big EXPORT SELECTED button. Under it are four collapsible sections:

  • Outputexport folder (with browse and open buttons), units, file naming (Component - Item.dxf or just Item.dxf), overwrite or auto-number, and whether to open the folder afterward.
  • Sketches & faceswhether to include construction lines, sketch points, and projected geometry.
  • Flat patternsbend lines, extent lines, and spline-to-polyline conversion with a tolerance.
  • Last exporteach file written, with its curve count and size, plus any skipped items and the reason.
Errors show in the panelIf an export fails, the reason appears in Last export, which opens by itself when something didn't export. Anything unexpected from Fusion shows in a red strip at the top of the panel; click the strip to dismiss it.
03UnitsFusion API▶

Units are a real option, not a workaround. I checked the API on your machine. Fusion has a newer sketch-export call with a units setting, and test exports in mm and inches each came out with the correct unit header. That call is marked "preview" by Autodesk, so if a future Fusion removes it, the add-in falls back to the old save method, which uses design units.

Units optionExport callResultUnit header in file
MillimeterscreateDXFSketchExportOptions, units = mmExported, 2,102 bytes$INSUNITS = 4 (millimeters)
InchescreateDXFSketchExportOptions, units = inExported, 2,054 bytes$INSUNITS = 1 (inches)
Design unitsThe Units menu's first choice, Design units, leaves the setting alone so the file uses whatever the design is set to. The helm control plug design is in inches, which is why the manual export earlier tonight came out in inches.
04Things to KnowNotes▶
  • ConstructionConstruction geometry is off by default, which suits laser and CNC. You can change this in Sketches & faces.
  • SplinesSplines-to-polylines only works for flat patterns. The sketch export has no such option.
  • Curved facesOnly planar faces can be exported. A curved face is listed in Last export as skipped, with the reason "not planar".
  • Partial sketchesIf you select only some curves of a sketch, the file gets "(selected)" added to its name so it can't be confused with a whole-sketch export.
05Not Yet TestedCaveat▶

Not yet tested live: the face path and the partial-sketch path, both of which use a temporary sketch. My test run hit your Untitled document, which had nothing selected, so those two paths never ran. Nothing was changed. Once the add-in is installed, select a planar face and a few curves of a sketch and export them. If either fails, the reason will show in Last export or in the red strip at the top of the panel.

Export pathStatusEvidence
Whole sketchVerifiedFour sketches exported from the helm control plug design, plus the mm and inch unit tests
Units settingVerifiedCorrect unit header for mm and inches
Partial sketchUntestedUses a temporary sketch; not yet run live
Planar faceUntestedUses a temporary sketch; not yet run live
Flat patternUntestedUses Fusion's built-in flat-pattern export; no sheet-metal part was open to test it
Temporary sketchesEach temporary sketch is deleted right after its file is written, even if the export fails, so the timeline ends up unchanged.
06Install & ShortcutSetup▶
Download the latest versionAlways the newest ExportSelectedToDXF.zip; the link never changes.ExportSelectedToDXF.zip
All versions and release notesEvery release on GitHub, newest first.github.com/…/releases
#TopicStep
1Unzip & installUnzip the file and double-click install-macos.command. On first run, macOS may need you to right-click it and choose Open.
2Run in FusionIn Fusion, press Shift+S, choose ExportSelectedToDXF under Add-Ins, and click Run. It will also run automatically each time Fusion starts.
Where the button isIn the DESIGN workspace, the button appears in two places: SOLID ▸ CREATE (at the bottom of the menu) and UTILITIES ▸ ADD-INS. Both open the same panel.
Keyboard shortcutRight-click the toolbar button, choose Change Keyboard Shortcut, and press your key combination. Your settings are stored outside the add-in folder, so reinstalling keeps them.
  • WindowsDouble-click install-windows.cmd instead. It runs install-windows.ps1, which copies the add-in into Fusion's AddIns folder.
  • Settings fileOn a Mac, settings live in ~/Library/Application Support/SwamiFusionAddins/ExportSelectedToDXF/settings.json; on Windows, in the same folder under %APPDATA%.
  • ReinstallingRun the installer again. It replaces the add-in folder but leaves the settings file alone.
07What You Can SelectFeature▶

You can select any mix of these in the canvas or the browser. Everything is sorted out at export time, and each item becomes its own file.

You selectHow it's exportedFile name (Component - Item)
Every curve of a sketchTreated as the whole sketch and exported directlyFRAME (DXF) - frame(dxf)-center.dxf
A sketch in the browserExported directlyComponent - sketch name.dxf
Some curves of a sketchProjected into a temporary sketch on the same plane, exported, then deletedComponent - sketch name (selected).dxf
A planar faceTemporary sketch on the face, face edges projected, exported, then deletedComponent - body face 1.dxf
A flat patternFusion's flat-pattern DXF exportComponent - Flat Pattern.dxf
A sheet-metal body, component or occurrenceIts flat pattern is exported, if it has oneComponent - Flat Pattern.dxf
Anything elseSkipped, with the reason shown in Last export—
No overwrites by defaultIf a file with the same name already exists, the new one gets -2, -3 and so on. Turn on Overwrite existing files in the Output section to replace instead.

09Package ContentsSetup▶

The zip, ExportSelectedToDXF-v1.0.0.zip, holds one folder. The .py and .manifest names must match the folder name, or Fusion won't list the add-in.

FileWhat it does
ExportSelectedToDXF.pyThe add-in: toolbar button, palette, export logic, settings and reset
ExportSelectedToDXF.manifestTells Fusion the name, version 1.0.0, and that it runs on startup on Mac and Windows
palette.htmlThe dark panel itself; works offline
resources/commandThe toolbar icon at 16, 32 and 64 pixels: a sheet with an arrow pointing out
install-macos.commandDouble-click installer for macOS
install-windows.cmdDouble-click installer for Windows; runs the PowerShell script
install-windows.ps1Copies the add-in into Fusion's AddIns folder on Windows
Preflight checksBefore delivery the package passed five preflight checks: the Python compiles, the macOS installer's shell syntax is valid, the file names match the folder, no template placeholders are left, and the version agrees between the .py and the manifest.
10How the Export WorksFusion API▶

Each export path uses a specific Fusion API call. These were looked up in the API documentation inside your Fusion (version 2706.1.17).

PathAPI callWhat it controls
SketchExportManager.createDXFSketchExportOptionsUnits, construction geometry, sketch points, projected geometry
Sketch fallbackSketch.saveAsDXFNothing; design units and all geometry
Face or partial sketchSketches.add, then Sketch.project2 (unlinked), then the sketch export, then deleteMeSame as a sketch
Flat patternExportManager.createDXFFlatPatternExportOptionsUnits, bend center lines, bend extent lines, spline-to-polyline conversion and tolerance
Preview featureAutodesk marks createDXFSketchExportOptions as a preview feature that may change. If it ever stops working, the add-in quietly switches to saveAsDXF, which still exports but ignores the Units and Sketches & faces options.
Live selection countThe add-in listens for Fusion's selection-changed event, so the count at the top of the panel updates as you click. It only does this while the panel is visible.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
PaletteFusion UIA dockable HTML panel inside Fusion that stays open while you work, unlike a modal command dialog.
Add-inFusion UIA Python program that loads into Fusion, can run at startup, and adds its own buttons and panels.
DXFExportDrawing Exchange Format, the 2D file format most laser, plasma and CNC software reads.
Sketch curveGeometryA line, arc, circle or spline inside a sketch.
Planar faceGeometryA flat face of a solid body. Only planar faces can be laid flat in a DXF.
Flat patternSheet MetalThe unfolded 2D layout of a sheet-metal part, with its bends shown as lines.
Sheet metalSheet MetalFusion's tools for modeling bent parts from flat stock of a set thickness.
Bend linesSheet MetalLines on a flat pattern showing where to bend: center lines mark the middle of each bend, extent lines mark where it starts and ends.
Construction geometryGeometryReference curves in a sketch, shown dashed, used for layout but not meant to be cut.
Projected geometryGeometryCurves copied into a sketch from edges, faces or other sketches. Unlinked projections become ordinary curves.
Sketch pointsGeometryStandalone points in a sketch, such as hole centers.
SplineGeometryA smooth freeform curve. Some CAM and laser software handles splines poorly.
PolylineGeometryA chain of short straight segments that approximates a curve within a set tolerance.
Temporary sketchExportA sketch the add-in creates only to hold geometry for one export, then deletes.
Unit headerExportThe $INSUNITS entry in a DXF file that tells other software which unit the coordinates are in.
Design unitsExportThe default length unit set in a design's Document Settings.
Fusion APIAPIAutodesk's programming interface that add-ins and scripts use to control Fusion.
createDXFSketchExportOptionsAPIThe newer API call for exporting a sketch to DXF, with settings for units and which geometry to include.
saveAsDXFAPIThe original API call for saving a sketch as DXF. Autodesk has retired it, but it still works.
createDXFFlatPatternExportOptionsAPIThe API call for exporting a flat pattern to DXF, with bend-line and spline options.
Preview featureAPIAn API call Autodesk has released early and may change or remove in a later version.
Preflight checksInstallAutomatic checks run on the package before delivery to catch broken code, mismatched names and leftover placeholders.
ManifestInstallThe small file Fusion reads to list an add-in: its name, version, supported systems and whether it runs on startup.
InstallerInstallA double-click script that copies the add-in folder into Fusion's AddIns folder.
Settings fileInstallA per-user file, kept outside the add-in folder, that remembers your options between sessions and reinstalls.
TimelineFusion UIThe history bar at the bottom of a Fusion design that records every feature and sketch in order.
CNCExportComputer numerical control: machines such as routers and mills that cut from toolpaths.
